newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes illegal fishing charges vs Chinese.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes illegal fishing charges vs Chinese.

text.p: Twenty-three Chinese fishermen arrested in an area claimed by Manila in the disputed Spratly Islands will probably be charged will illegal fishing, a senior Philippine official said on Wednesday.
"We are dealing with suspected violators of the law," foreign undersecretary Rodolfo Severino told reporters.

The Philippine Navy said in a statement that the Chinese were on a board Hong Kong-registered vessel identified as the Cheng Lun Yau when they were apprehended on July 31 near Hasa-Hasa Shoal. A second fishing vessel sighted in the area sped away, it said.
"They were found to have dynamite. I believe they had also fish...so they will probably be charged with illegal fishing," Severino said.
He said the Chinese embassy had not asked Manila to release the fishermen.
The Spratlys are a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, reefs and shoals in the South China Sea, some or all of which are claimed by China, the Philippines, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.
Beijing says all the islands and rocky outcrops in the sea have been Chinese territory since ancient times.

A recent series of incidents involving alleged trespassing by Chinese naval and fishing vessels in areas claimed by Manila in the South China Sea has strained relations between China and the Philippines.

The Philippine Navy in May arrested 21 Chinese fishermen near Scarborough Shoal, well north of the Spratlys, for alleged illegal entry. But a local judge ordered their release from 52 days detention, saying ownership of the shoal had not been established.
